title: Octahedral connectivity as a design principle in perovskite oxides for catalytic applications
content: Octahedral connectivity, the dimensionality and mode by which BO6 polyhedra are connected across a perovskite lattice, is a dynamic, tunable, and structural descriptor. The electronic structure, defect formation, charge transport anisotropy, surface termination chemistry, and, ultimately, catalytic function of perovskite oxides are significantly influenced by their octahedral connectivity. While simple perovskites feature corner-sharing BO6 networks in three dimensions, their low-dimensional analogues, spanning two-dimensional (2D), one-dimensional (1D), and zero-dimensional (0D) frameworks, with corner-sharing, edge-sharing, face-sharing, or isolated octahedra, offer new opportunities to tailor structure–property relationships. Reducing connectivity from 3D to 0D systematically decreases oxygen vacancy formation energy, introduces structural anisotropy and ordered vacancy channels, and produces B-site coordination environments that allow catalytic functions inaccessible in the fully connected 3D parent structure. This review systematically examines the diversity of octahedral connectivity across perovskite oxide-based materials, containing different connection modes. We analyze how these structural motifs influence defect chemistry and interfacial behavior, with a focus on oxygen vacancies, cation non-stoichiometry, and octahedral connectivity. We further connect these structural and chemical characteristics with photocatalytic and electrocatalytic performance in water splitting and CO2 reduction and extend this connectivity-informed framework to thermocatalytic biomass valorization, highlighting design principles that link octahedral connectivity to catalytic function. Critically, we establish that the eg orbital occupancy descriptor effective for 3D ABO3 electrocatalysts loses analytical power in structurally anisotropic layered derivatives, highlighting the need for connectivity-specific descriptors. This review aims to guide the rational development of perovskite oxide catalysts across photo-, electro-, and thermocatalytic applications through connectivity- and defect-informed strategies.
